model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, Tom Sell's overwhelming financial advantage over Kyle Rable, and prediction-market pricing near 97 percent Republican all point to a safe GOP hold despite Arrington's retirement.
model.watch: Only an extraordinary national wave or a major scandal on the Republican side could put the outcome in doubt, and even then the margin would likely remain wide.

overview:
TX-19 covers West Texas, including Lubbock and Abilene, and has voted heavily Republican in recent cycles, with a partisan lean of roughly 25 points toward the GOP. With Jodey Arrington retiring, the seat is open, but the Republican side of the ballot remains strongly favored. Tom Sell has raised about $2.5 million and benefits from roughly $1.3 million in outside support, while Democrat Kyle Rable has raised under $50,000 with minimal cash on hand.

No public general-election polls are available and no expert raters have flagged the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and spending patterns. Prediction markets price the Republican nominee's chances near 97 percent. Even with the incumbent off the ballot, the combination of a deep red electorate, a large financial edge, and a low-profile race makes a Democratic upset highly unlikely.
